clue.text: See 10
Heath's Australian cousin writing a letter that's brief and pungent

parts.note: an epistle is a letter in writing, and EP is its brief form, the abbreviation
acrid means sharp and pungent in smell or taste

explanation.surface: A short, sharp-tongued letter written by an Australian relative of a man called Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath looks like a surname (Edward Heath, the politician) but is the plant. Ep. is the standard abbreviation for epistle.
explanation.definitionFit: An epacrid is a shrub of a mainly Australian plant family closely related to the heathers of the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Here and there, maybe

parts.note: the phrase itself is made up of a particular count of words, and that count is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like it means 'scattered about', but count its words: there are three. As a bonus, the word 'there' rearranged gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'here and there' consists of exactly that number of words, so a count of them gives this number.

clue.text: "Make me a lord" assigned to 9 but not 15

indicators.note: to make something is to form or construct it, so the following letters are built into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, all seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pleading for a peerage, which went to one prime minister but not another.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was made Earl Attlee in 1955; Winston Churchill declined a peerage and stayed in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of earl was granted to Attlee on retirement, while Churchill turned down such honours, so it fits one and not the other.

clue.text: Where fighter pilot is to die, holding back old lawyer

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to cop it is slang for to be killed or die

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so this short abbreviation is written right to left

parts.note: a King's Counsel; in 1999 the title was QC, so KC was the old one

explanation.surface: A wartime airman faces death while carrying an ageing barrister in his plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A cock is a fighting bird, so a cockpit is also the pit where cockfights were held, as well as a pilot's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment of an aircraft where the pilot sits; it was also the arena for fighting cocks.

clue.text: A greater lord in a play, with other ranks in the circle

definitions.text: A greater lord in a play

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, plural here
taken as written
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A nobleman in a drama mixing with ordinary soldiers in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; a duke is a greater lord than the earl of 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is a duke, the highest rank of the peerage, appearing in Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Decisive blow to a party audience native to Australia

parts.note: a knockout, the blow that ends a boxing match
taken as written
short for the Labour Party
to give someone an ear is to grant them a hearing

explanation.surface: A knockout punch delivered to a gathering of spectators at a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a tree-dwelling marsupial found only in eastern Australia, so it is an Australian native.

clue.text: I shall make bequests with malice

parts.note: the contraction I'll
to will property is to leave it in a testament

explanation.surface: Someone promising to write their testament out of spite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe hostility or a wish for harm towards another person, a feeling of spite.

clue.text: Prime Minister and a hundred people gossip in shelter …

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the people and their gossip go within the shelter

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
men as people in general
to tattle is to chatter or tell tales

explanation.surface: A national leader and a crowd chatting while taking cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The shelter splits L-E...E around the people and their gossip. The answer's first name, Clement, feeds the theme: Lady Churchill was Clementine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led the Labour government as the UK's head of government from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: ,1,12 9 (part1) finder revealed as not one indeed?

definitions.note: the proverb says a friend in need is a friend indeed; this sort of companion is not that kind

parts.note: the first part of 9-down is CLEMENT, which describes mild, pleasant conditions outdoors, so it stands for a two-word phrase meaning just that

indicators.note: revealed suggests the word finder being opened up and shown in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who discovers what Clement Attlee was, unmasked as not a true companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 9 (part 1) as the first word of 9-down's answer, CLEMENT, standing for mild, pleasant weather. The definition plays on the proverb 'a friend in need is a friend indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion who sticks by you only in good times is the opposite of the proverb's true ally in need.

clue.text: Savoury for the dinner Elisha blessed

parts.note: the letters run across the end of dinner, all of Elisha and the start of blessed

explanation.surface: A tasty dish, fit for the meal the prophet Elisha blessed.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no signal word for the hidden answer; the biblical surface (Elisha's miracles with food in 2 Kings) carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be relished is tasty and appetising, which is what savoury means as an adjective.

clue.text: See 10
Like Lady 15, a senior civil servant

definitions.note: a comparison: the fruit is like a clementine
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Lady Churchill was Clementine, and a clementine is a small citrus fruit of this kind
second meaning: a powerful official, originally in imperial China

explanation.walkthrough: Lady 15 is Clementine Churchill, Winston's wife; her name is also a fruit, and several clues use her as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus fruit is a close relative of the clementine, and the word is also slang for a top-ranking government official.

clue.text: Extraction possibly due to Bond?

indicators.note: possibly hints at another arrangement than the one written, so the short word before it is reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
cement is what bonds bricks together

explanation.surface: A spy-film question: could a removal be the work of James Bond?
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like the secret agent; it is a binding material.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to draw out or extract, so the noun formed from it names the act of drawing something out.

clue.text: … one before and after finding Christians unhealthy

parts.note: the church is the body of Christian believers
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Continuing from 9: someone discovering that believers are sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this to 9: Winston Churchill was Prime Minister before Attlee (1940-45) and again after him (1951-55).
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill held the premiership in the years either side of Attlee's government, so he preceded and followed him.

clue.text: Saint 9 (part 1)'s say 29 and 25s — they sound pretty

indicators.note: sound points to how a word is heard when spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: belles are pretty women

explanation.surface: Quoting the nursery rhyme about a London church, and remarking how nice they are to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'Oranges and lemons, say the bells of St Clement's' (29 and 25 supply the fruit).
explanation.definitionFit: In the old nursery rhyme it is the church peals of St Clement's that ring out the words about citrus fruit.

clue.text: The baby is a girl

parts.note: taken as written
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Announcing the sex of a newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means offspring or children, as in 'died without issue', so a baby is someone's offspring.

clue.text: Like Lady 15, came off the wheel in Japan

definitions.note: a comparison: the fruit is like a clementine
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small citrus fruit akin to the clementine, Lady Churchill's first name

definitions.text: came off the wheel in Japan
definitions.note: describes the pottery, a verb phrase for a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Japanese ware thrown on a potter's wheel

explanation.walkthrough: 'Came off the wheel' suggests a crash; it means pottery thrown on a potter's wheel. Satsuma ware is a cream-glazed pottery from the former Satsuma province.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a loose-skinned mandarin-type fruit and a decorated earthenware made in a southern Japanese province.

clue.text: Spike swallowing wrath, like Lady 15

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a tine is a prong or spike, as on a fork
wrath is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A sharp point taking in fury, compared to a titled woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is a deep-orange variety of mandarin, a near relation of the clementine named after Lady Churchill.

clue.text: Roof beam on top of gable needs hard worker

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: only the opening letter is kept
a rafter is a sloping beam supporting a roof

explanation.surface: A builder's observation that putting a beam on a gable takes a diligent labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Grafter is British slang for someone who works hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To graft in British slang is to toil, so the one who toils is a diligent, industrious labourer.

clue.text: Recovered from the Nile, egg without proper covering?

definitions.note: describes the state of someone in the garment, an adjective phrase

indicators.note: recovered can be read as covered anew, given a fresh form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An egg fished out of the river Nile, not properly wrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: A négligé is a flimsy dressing gown, or the state of being informally or scantily dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in négligé is in a state of undress, lightly or carelessly clothed rather than properly dressed.

clue.text: See 27
Keep cannabis in the kitchen?

definitions.note: loose: names where the thing is found rather than the thing

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them for sale
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone hiding drugs among the kitchen cupboards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a large cooking vessel for simmering bones and vegetables into broth, a fixture of any kitchen.

clue.text: Assert a member to be in liquor

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the limb goes inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Claiming that a club member is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club, and 'in liquor' suggests drunk; the member is a limb and the liquor is beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege something is to claim or declare it is true, typically without yet proving it.

clue.text: The sole possible answer and it's no good

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that goes with sole to name a flatfish
second meaning: slang for a dud, something that fails to work

explanation.walkthrough: 'The sole possible answer' reads as 'the only answer'; sole is the fish, and lemon sole is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon sole is a common edible flatfish, and a lemon is also slang for a faulty purchase, especially a car.

clue.text: Mentally without help — it's about making one generous

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so what remains goes round the next piece
without means lacking, so a word for support is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
an ally is a helper or supporter
unific is a rare adjective meaning making into one, unifying

explanation.surface: A comment on someone who, unaided in their mind, set out to make a person kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without help' reads like 'unaided', but help is a word to take away; unific is a rare word, found mainly in dictionaries, for unifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Munificent describes someone who gives lavishly, so it is a more formal word for liberal and open-handed.

clue.text: ,22 A tide at sea may help to give time

parts.note: the main is the open sea, a poetic usage
a spring tide is the high tide near new and full moon

explanation.surface: Tides out at sea could serve to tell the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainspring is the coiled driving spring in a clock or watch, the part that powers its timekeeping.

clue.text: Drawing of a man holding a Unionist prisoner

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the man wraps round the rest

parts.note: he is a man, by pronoun
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for Unionist
a lag is a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A sketch of a man keeping an Ulster Unionist captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests a picture, but here it means pulling. A Unionist favours Northern Ireland staying in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the business of pulling or carrying goods, and to draw a load is to haul it.

clue.text: Nothing extends from Lady 15's big brothers

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a thing that ranges extends or stretches over an area

explanation.surface: Nothing reaches beyond a titled woman's elder siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger citrus fruits are the bigger relatives of the small clementine, Lady Churchill's first name, hence its big brothers.
